steps.message: client.py isn't staging-only — `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`. An unconditional `verify=False` there would silently disable TLS verification for the nightly production export too, not just staging.

questions.question: client.py is shared by sync_staging.py and export_prod.py. How should verify=False be scoped?

options.label: Env-gated (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default true) and pass verify=<flag> on both calls. Staging sets it to false; production keeps verification on. Same one-line fix at the call sites, no prod exposure.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Point verify= at the staging cert file instead of disabling it. Keeps verification on everywhere, but needs the self-signed cert checked in or on disk.

options.label: Unconditional verify=False
options.description: Exactly as asked: verify=False on both calls in client.py. Production export also stops verifying certs and becomes MITM-able.

Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17`.

Two things worth knowing:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same client against `https://reports.example.com`, so the nightly finance export now accepts any certificate. Say the word and I'll env-gate it.
- **Expect log noise.** urllib3 emits an `InsecureRequestWarning` per call. If it's noisy, `urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)` silences it — I left it out since you didn't ask.
